title: Say the same finish in the agent prompt and the human loop
lead: `docs/agents.md` has two implement procedures. The copy-paste prompt always records handoff and says to run done only after review and merge. The pickup paragraph below it says done and then `slicer check`. Getting started shows both paths without saying that `implement_finish` chooses.
findings_note: the implement prompt always hands off, while the human loop later shows done and does not say which finish the project uses
boundary: **Not in this slice:** `ai.py`, the skill, or `AGENTS.md`; changing what `implement_finish` does (s186); `LOOP` command strings (s177).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A person reading getting started, and an agent copying the implement prompt, do not get the finish `slicer ai instructions` prints. This repo finishes with done. A handoff project finishes with handoff. The prompt and the human loop should name that choice instead of each picking one.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_ImplementPrompt_FollowsThePrintedFinish`: the `### Implement one slice` prompt contains `slicer ai instructions`, `implement_finish`, `slicer done ID`, and `slicer handoff ID`. The phrase `only after review and merge` occurs only after the handoff command, as the handoff case. Existing assertions in `test_Instructions_UseOneCallSliceReadPath_AndPreserveReadBeforeStart` still pass: the prompt still reads scope before `slicer start ID`, still says to resolve an ambiguous specification first, and still uses the bounded `next --ready` pickup.
2. The pickup paragraph that begins with the slicer next queue sentence says the default finish is `slicer done ID --note "..." --render` followed by `slicer check`, and that an `implement_finish` of `handoff` uses the handoff command from `slicer ai instructions` instead.
3. In `docs/getting-started.md`, the handoff example says to use it when `implement_finish` is `handoff`. Section `6. The loop` names `slicer ai instructions` as the agent loop, says the short example is the default done finish, and the `start` and `done` examples in that section include `--render`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Rewrite only the finish sentences of the implement prompt. Keep the pickup, the specification check, `slicer start ID --render --strict`, the tracking-CLI rule, and the ban on committing unless authorized.

Once verified, run step 4 of `slicer ai instructions`. That is `slicer done ID --note "Describe the verified outcome" --render` unless `implement_finish` is `handoff`, in which case it is `slicer handoff ID --render`. Then run `slicer check`. When step 4 was handoff, run done only after review and merge.

Add the same choice to the pickup paragraph. Do not copy a `--check` flag; s177 owns that.

In getting started, label the existing handoff block and section 6 as the two finishes. Add `--render` to the section 6 `start` and `done` examples. Do not rewrite the rest of the tutorial.

CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]`, `### Changed`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the changelog entry.
